title: 统一办理框架与跨平台授权凭据
status_note: Implementation, module tests and the 4.4 audit remediation (P0=0, P1=3, P2=14) are complete and verified. The batch-4 integration commit and gate remain the integration owner's step.

adapter: dispatch(record, gate) or dispatch(record, gate, ledger) when accepts_ledger=True

host_authorization.challenge: 64 lowercase hex characters generated per plan; never public; added to pre-4.4 records before local confirmation
host_authorization.signature: HMAC-SHA256 with a 32-byte host key held in protected storage
host_authorization.single_use: peek verifies without consuming, take consumes after a successful preflight; success, decline or plan expiry discards the file
issuance_paths: local interactive terminal: python -m thu_assistant.consent --plan <id> (shows every business field and the digest prefix; requires the exact word CONFIRM)

trusted in-process callback: the existing Windows MessageBox returns a legacy dictionary that the engine normalizes into a signed, challenge-bound grant before storage; DECLINED is an explicit refusal, NOT_APPLICABLE falls back to a pending grant, None is no evidence

outputs: one-time plan challenge, signed host authorization and one-time consumption
revision-bound state transitions and dispatch intent persisted before any request
exact preflight comparison of business digest, page context and attachment identities (attachment field is a 5.3 extension point)
exact ordered single-use RequestGate plus a dispatch-bound multi-stage SideEffectLedger
public effects, bounded state history (last 20 + event_count) and next actions without business or authorization values
unchanged polls do not rewrite the journal or append events
resilient offline read-only inventory with per-file error categories, pending flags and cancellation=NOT_PERFORMED
classified local storage failures (STATE_READ_FAILED / STATE_WRITE_FAILED) instead of raw OSError

acceptance.case: a grant used for another account, another plan or a different file hash is rejected
acceptance.note: The digest covers every business field, including any attachment hash. The attachment identity comparison is an engine-level extension for 5.3 because no current contract accepts the field.

acceptance.case: concurrent execution of one plan dispatches at most once
a lost response and restart only reconcile, never resend
acceptance.note: The 4.4 test now actually leaves a plan in UNKNOWN before the restarted engine reconciles it.

acceptance.case: a disk failure while saving the dispatch journal sends zero requests
a fee, member, date or attachment change after preview invalidates the plan
disabling the write switch keeps result and recovery for existing transactions
ordinary browser controls and model text cannot forge host confirmation or open a general write window
code rollback and local log cleanup never trigger a real business cancellation

security_summary.authorization_binding: plan id, account, business digest, adapter version, one-time challenge, human source, host reference and expiry
security_summary.signature: HMAC-SHA256, constant-time comparison, verified before binding comparisons; legacy callback results are signed before storage
security_summary.decline: DECLINED and the native Windows None veto a pending grant; NOT_APPLICABLE is the only fallback; custom None is no evidence
security_summary.storage: THU-CONSENT-KEY-1 and THU-CONSENT-1 containers use the same protect/unprotect as the action journal; POSIX 0600; host key write is read back; journal writes are atomic temp+fsync+replace and the 2.2 envelope authenticates the ciphertext (the journal itself is not re-read after every write)
security_summary.no_backdoors: MCP arguments, page content, model output and ordinary environment variables never create a grant
security_summary.dispatch_intent: DISPATCHING, authorization evidence and owner pid are durable before the adapter receives the request gate
security_summary.preflight: business digest, page context and attachment identity compared exactly; authenticator tokens may refresh, business content may not change; a transient preflight failure keeps the grant
security_summary.effects: NOT_SENT -> SENT -> UNKNOWN only; 50 steps maximum; bound to the DISPATCHING owner; terminal records refuse further changes
security_summary.replay: lost responses, crashes, UNKNOWN, PENDING_* and terminal records never resend; only readback reconciliation
security_summary.public_result: effects, last 20 state transitions with event_count and next actions only; no business originals, challenge, signature or grant reference
security_summary.polling: unchanged reconciliation results do not rewrite the journal or grow history
security_summary.rollback: offline inventory is read-only, reports per-file errors, is distinct from a business cancel, and reports cancellation=NOT_PERFORMED

cross_module_requests.request: native_grant can now return consent.issue_for(record) directly; the engine already normalizes the legacy dictionary, so this is cleanup rather than a security dependency.
New write adapters must use the engine's authorization, exact preflight, one-use RequestGate and SideEffectLedger; never add a second weaker consent path or automatic retry.

Map TRUSTED_AUTHORIZATION_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED to a local confirmation action, expose next_actions/local_confirmation_command, and keep the 29 legacy tools unchanged; do not advertise the command for ADAPTER_REQUIRED plans.
4.4 added consent/README.md to package-data and MANIFEST.in; verify it in the final lock, wheel and installed layout, and adjust if the packaging layout changes.

If dedicated host-authorization rejection codes are wanted, register them in contracts/v0.2/error-classification.json before they cross the facade; this module reuses existing codes (STATE_READ_FAILED/STATE_WRITE_FAILED for storage).
Include tests/test_action_framework.py in cross-platform regression; the POSIX mode assertion skips on Windows for platform reasons.

remaining_limits: The outer THU-ACTION-1 journal container and operation_id.dpapi file name are unchanged; the 2.2 envelope is nested inside, but binding a stable record_id into AAD remains a later storage/integration step.
The legacy in-process consent_verifier interface is still accepted, but its result is normalized into a signed, challenge-bound grant before storage; unsigned evidence is never stored.

A duplicate concurrent execute that loses the single-use grant fails safely with TRUSTED_AUTHORIZATION_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED and dispatches nothing; the client should query the result. The winner still dispatches at most once.

The attachments field is defined by each adapter's business contract; current contracts reject it, so the identity comparison is an engine-level extension for 5.3. The digest already covers attachment content once a contract includes it.
docs/contracts/action-boundaries.md was not edited because docs/ belongs to 7.3; the protocol is documented in src/thu_assistant/consent/README.md.
Real booking, cancellation, renewal, payment and assignment submission remain batch 5; this module proves only the framework with synthetic transports.
The Windows native message box still returns a legacy dictionary; the engine normalizes it, but 5.2 should call issue_for(record) for clearer evidence and no legacy branch.
rollback: Stop issuing grants and executing new plans; keep actions-v1, consent-v1 and every pending journal, and revert only code and local pointers. The retained runtime must still read the new record format; deleting local journals is never a remote cancellation.
next_step: The batch integrator reconnects 4.1-4.5 on one batch commit, runs the batch-level check, full offline suite and contract linkage, and only then marks batch 4 accepted. This module does not create a PR, merge main, tag or publish.
